body.statement: For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\), \(P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge 1-\alpha\) at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design. The bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions. Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\); equivalently, the local profile boundary and the Wald ellipse have the same first-order quadratic expansion and \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) calibration. At any law with a non-singleton identified set or without the separated-chart conditions, the theorem asserts coverage only and makes no claim that \(\operatorname{diam}(K_n)\) shrinks.
body.justification: Exact nuisance calibration preserves coverage at transitions, while the explicit Hausdorff comparison recovers ordinary Wald geometry on separated charts.
body.gap: Existing weak-identification and stable-bound procedures do not calibrate a profile discrepancy over this changing selected-SCM fiber or establish its first-order agreement with chart-specific Wald inference.
body.consumer: Boundary-sensitive PN/PS analyses receive honest uncertainty without interpreting a nonshrinking confidence fiber as point identification.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniform first-order Hausdorff equivalence between the exact confidence-fiber inversion and the selected Wald ellipse for the globally defined atlas.
obligation.obstruction: Exact coverage does not require rank stability, but the global Hausdorff assertion requires both a uniform glued-chart likelihood expansion and proof that no mixed-support component is omitted near the true law.
obligation.attempted: Proved exact Berger--Boos coverage from the preliminary-region event and discrete super-uniform tail values, and reduced the separated smooth local case to the profile-Wald quadratic conditional on atlas exhaustiveness.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(q_0\) be the true observable law and let \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\).  Exact inversion of each binomial tail and the stated Bonferroni allocation imply
\[
P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}\le\beta_n.
\]
For a fixed compatible pair \((q,t)\), put
\[
G_{q,t}
=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
The randomized variable is not needed: the ordinary upper-tail value is super-uniform even at atoms, so
\[
P_q\{G_{q,t}\le u\}\le u,
\qquad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Because \(t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0)\), on \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\) the supremum defining \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\) includes \(q_0\), whence
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)
\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}.
\]
Using \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2\), it follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
&\le P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}
  +P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}\\
&\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves exact finite-sample coverage and remains valid along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\).  On a locally exhaustive separated smooth chart, the multinomial likelihood has the usual uniform quadratic expansion, and the common incident Jacobian reduces the target profile to the Wald quadratic; this gives \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\) under that local premise.  The stated global Hausdorff conclusion still requires a uniform glued-chart profile expansion and proof that no mixed-support component is omitted near the true law.
